architecture: Exclusive Web Lock gates playback; BroadcastChannel targets owner epochs and remote Pause requests. Transfer callback pauses audio synchronously before releasing. No server coordinator or widened network policy. Fixed/country resources versioned.
complexity: Coordinator is proportionate to approved design; fixes should preserve lock-based exclusion and strengthen controller attempt/event handling, not redesign the architecture.
correctness: Independent focused local repros show stale play continuation stops a newer attempt and actual media pause retains ownership with playing UI. These violate predictable rapid-action recovery and ownership release on paused playback.

findings.problem: The stale-attempt branch calls audio.pause() unconditionally even when a newer playback attempt owns the same audio element. A delayed old play fulfillment can silence the newly resumed stream while wanted remains true and UI remains playing.
findings.requested_change: Ensure old attempt continuations cannot mutate the shared audio element or current state after ownership/attempt changes. Add regression for delayed fulfillment after newer Play and restore meaningful late completion/rejection coverage.

findings.evidence: /tmp/dial004-review-repro.mjs second test: start and settle playback; invoke audio.pause() to deliver media pause event; after settling lock remains active and UI playing.
findings.problem: The pause handler updates state only when wanted is already false. A media/browser-driven pause while wanted is true leaves coordinator ownership and heartbeat active and UI falsely playing. Approved contract requires releasing ownership after audio is paused.
findings.requested_change: Handle genuine current media pause by canceling intent and releasing ownership after audio has stopped, while guarding against late old-source pause events affecting a newer attempt. Add regression verifying paused state and lock release.
